dwp_take: Google and Mozilla have revoked trust in eight intermediate certificates from Indian certificate authority eMudhra after the company's private keys were compromised, meaning attackers could potentially forge legitimate-looking certificates to impersonate websites and services. This matters because certificate authorities are the foundation of web security, and when they fail, every organization relying on HTTPS and SSL/TLS encryption is theoretically at risk until patches roll out. Here's the thing: eMudhra probably isn't the household name that keeps your CISO up at night, but this is exactly why you can't just buy a certificate and forget about it, and why those browser updates your users keep ignoring are actually worth the five minutes of inconvenience.
